build: stop Pages running a static prototype through Jekyll
entries.body:
This site is plain static HTML — there is no _config.yml, no front matter in
any page, and nothing here wants Liquid. Pages was building it with Jekyll
anyway, because that is the default for a branch source without .nojekyll.

Two consequences, one silent and one loud. Silent: Jekyll drops paths starting
with an underscore, so _seed.html was never published. Loud: it walks and
copies all 327 files, including ~70 MB of preview PNGs and .fig binaries, and
every deployment since this push has entered in_progress and been killed at
the ten-minute timeout.

.nojekyll makes Pages upload the tree as it stands.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: fix: stop the refresh job staging a path git is configured to refuse
entries.body:
The Chrome fix got the workflow all the way to its commit step, where it died
on `docs/usecases.md` and `docs/usecases`. Those are regenerated every run and
they are also ignored now — this repository is public and Pages serves it from
the branch, so the review apparatus stays untracked. An ignored path is not an
absent one: it exists on the runner, `git add` refuses it, and under `bash -e`
that takes the job down.

The helper now asks git what it will accept instead of carrying a second list
of what is ignored, so the next ignore rule cannot redden this job the same
way. Simulated locally against the real tree: 22 artifacts collected, both
docs paths skipped, exit 0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: fix: let every browser tool find Chrome where CI actually keeps it
entries.body:
The refresh workflow shipped in this push and ran for the first time. It sets
CHROME_PATH to the runner's Chrome, and only one of the four tools that drive
a browser was reading it — so the run got through the use-case captures and
then died in shoot-previews.js on a macOS path that cannot exist on a Linux
runner.

Three occurrences of one hardcoded string is the threshold for extracting it
rather than patching each: tools/chrome-path.js now resolves CHROME_PATH with
the macOS install as the fallback, so passing the variable stays optional on a
developer's machine. build-usecases.js keeps its own local name because the
capture path injects it as a dependency; only the resolution moved.

Verified by running the script that failed: it launches and writes its preview.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: chore: keep the review apparatus out of the published repository
entries.body:
This repository is public and Pages serves it from `main`, so committing a
file here publishes it under mateuszkoslacz.com. docs/, CLAUDE.md and
.review-lineage/ had never been pushed — they were untracked until this
session's loop committed them, and pushing would have put the conversion
analysis, the product owner's rulings and every finding raised against the
prototype on a public site, permanently and in history.

They are ignored now rather than merely absent, so the next round cannot
re-add them by accident, and the reason is written where someone about to
delete the rule will read it. The files stay on disk; nothing was lost.

changelog.json is rebuilt because the commits it described no longer exist.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: fix: style the control this round added, instead of letting the product paint it [IMPL-25]
entries.body:
IMPL-25 added a fifth control to the comment layer's toolbar and shipped no
CSS for it. Nobody noticed, because every check that round was behavioural —
hrefs, counts, gates, export mode, file://, the seam. The completeness critic
measured the thing itself and found it inheriting `--navy-500` from litro.css
at 16px weight 400, sitting between siblings at 12px weight 700 inside a
component whose own stylesheet header says it is "deliberately scaffolding,
never a product component". That coupling is precisely what the file exists to
prevent.

It also came out at 23.19px tall on desktop and 21.75px on mobile — the only
control in the toolbar below the 24x24 floor of WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8, which its
four siblings clear at 28px, and the 7px flex gap denies it the spacing
exception. It now states its own size and colour: 28px, 12px/700, the same
#9C7A12 border and 7px radius, measured on both surfaces.

One deliberate difference from the buttons: no fill. The way out of the layer
should not read as loud as the actions inside it.

Not fixed here, and worth an operator decision rather than a unilateral
redesign: a fifth always-on control grows the toolbar from 227x48 to 389x48 on
desktop, and on 390px it wraps to two rows at 354x83, covering more of the
screen and overlapping the mobile price bar. Styling shrinks it slightly; the
wrap is intrinsic to the control count.

proto-sheets.css's header still said two sheets while its module builds three.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: feat: let a reviewer reach the open-threads page from inside a screen [IMPL-25]
entries.body:
comments.html was linked from the hub and from nowhere else. The panel shipped
two content sheets, each carrying a .pt-sheet-page link to its full page, and
the comment layer's own toolbar carried four controls and no way out. So a
reviewer standing on a screen, looking at a pin, who wanted to know what else
was open had to navigate back to the hub to find out — which is the one
question the overview exists to answer.

Two routes now, because they answer at different moments. The panel gains a
third sheet, built like its siblings: the page link sits beside the sheet
rather than inside its redrawn body, which is what makes it survive every
redraw and failure path including file://. It has no changelog-like data to
list, so its body is a short bilingual statement of what the page is. And the
comment layer's toolbar gains a link built from pageBase(), never shareBase()
— the two-link rule this loop has now been bitten by twice.

Both inherit their exclusions structurally rather than by special case: the
toolbar is not built at all when the layer mounts in overview mode, and
neither surface exists under ?nopanel=1, which is what keeps a pin out of a
Figma frame.

This closes BC-3, the last red business criterion: all three review pages are
now reachable from the hub and from the panel, and each links back into the
screens or states it describes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: docs: say plainly that the live comment path cannot be verified here [IMPL-26]
entries.body:
One Definition of Done in this loop said "signed in on localhost, the page
still lists every thread". No automated actor in this repository can show
that: the rules admit only an allowlisted reviewer with a verified Google
email, FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT is unset and no key file exists. The round
that met it honestly marked the card partial. The next round would have marked
it met, because nothing here said the claim was unavailable.

The missing credential was never the defect. The silence about it was.

README now says which credential a live check needs, that its absence makes
the claim unverifiable rather than assumed-good, what the createFirebaseClient
seam does prove, and — the part worth the section on its own — that
init({store}) is a different seam that reports a vacuous zero updateDoc count,
the same zero correct code produces. A criterion measured that way passes
whether or not the code works.

It states the requirement and stops: no instructions for obtaining, storing or
committing a credential, and an explicit line that the allowlist is an
operator decision rather than the obstacle.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: fix: eight defects in the comment layer, most of them created by the round that fixed the last eight [IMPL-11..IMPL-18]
entries.body:
The overview's "open the pin" row was built from shareLink(), the one builder
that resolves against prototypeUrl — so on localhost every row walked the
reviewer off their own copy onto the published site. That is OP-01 again, at a
call site the round fixing OP-01 created, because the pageBase/shareBase rule
lived in a code comment and nowhere a later card would read it. The row is now
a deepLink; shareLink keeps its real job on a separate copy-link button.

The overview also: hung on "Loading" whenever the first delivery beat wire(),
because setThreads was resolved before the await and the catch-up was guarded
on a length that cannot distinguish an empty store from an unanswered one;
issued Firestore writes from a page that calls itself read-only, because
hiding the pins with display:none is not suppressing them — an overview flag
now short-circuits renderThreads and the CSS block is gone; and rendered a
confident link to nowhere for an unresolvable anchor, because deepLink never
throws and its on-a-screen fallback is comments.html here.

hydrate() captured history.replaceState afresh per batch, so two overlapping
batches left the native function permanently stubbed. It is an in-flight
counter now, and a failed detail fetch is retried instead of being remembered
as done.

Page identity is the whole path, not the basename, and needsRestore now agrees
with the render decision. A thread with no anchor.page still renders where its
selector resolves — that fallback is load-bearing for legacy threads — but no
longer flaps the store's orphaned flag as the reviewer walks between screens.

The popover's 18px chrome gutter is back on all four clamps, measured against
the layout viewport rather than innerWidth, so a classic scrollbar cannot
clamp it into itself. 252 assertions over 6 corners x 2 heights x 3 viewports.

comments.rules is untouched: the named-allowlist model is an operator decision.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: fix: stop a panel switch becoming NaN, and give the review pages copy a stakeholder can read [IMPL-23, IMPL-24]
entries.body:
?rooms= is read by two consumers: the numeric search state and the demo
panel's room-types-on-card axis. The search state coerced it unconditionally,
so ?rooms=on rendered "2 adulti, 2 copii, NaN camere" — on four of the
twenty-two use-case deep links, which is to say on the page built to
demonstrate the prototype's states. The axis is not renamed: ?rooms= is in the
URL register CLAUDE.md invariant #10 protects and live deep links carry it.
The coercion is narrowed instead, to a finite number, at both engines. All 22
deep links now render with no NaN and no Infinity; the panel axis still reads
on/off; a legitimate 0 still applies.

The changelog printed the data token "unreleased" as a heading on a Romanian
page while proto-sheets.js already mapped that exact value to "Nepublicat";
said "din primele 50" in Romanian against "of the latest 50" in English; and
ended all fifty cards with the commit trailer. The round label now comes from
one function shared by the heading and the jump nav, so they cannot disagree;
the Romanian half says "ultimele" with the 20+ "de" agreement; and the whole
trailer block is stripped at render time — changelog.json keeps it, all fifty
entries. A commit whose body is only a trailer renders no paragraph at all.

Two Romanian gender agreements fixed in usecases.html: clona is feminine.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: fix: make a hidden review-page control actually hide, and let a button be the primary affordance [IMPL-19, IMPL-20]
entries.body:
Two review-page stylesheet defects with the same shape: a rule at class
specificity deciding something an attribute or an element type should decide.

.rp-nav and .rp-toolbar set `display: flex`, which beats the UA sheet's
`[hidden] { display: none }`, so every page that toggles them through the
`hidden` attribute rendered them anyway — 36.9 px of jump nav on the changelog
and 34.9 px of live filter chips offered to a signed-out reviewer who has
nothing to filter. Both now measure 0 while hidden and unchanged when shown.

.rp-btn was typed to `a` alone, so comments.html's sign-in <button> — the only
call to action a signed-out reviewer sees — fell through to the UA grey
rgb(239,239,239). It is now the orange token, with the border, font and cursor
a button does not inherit on its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Give comments a page they can be read from, and the review round three pages it can be handed
entries.body:
A stakeholder comment was reachable only by finding its pin on the screen it was
written on. Nobody could see how many threads were open, what they said, or which
screens carried them — which is the question a workshop round opens with. The same
was true of the changelog and the product use cases: both existed, both were
readable only through a ~280 px sheet inside the floating panel.

So there are now three pages built for reading — changelog.html, usecases.html and
comments.html — linked from the hub and from the panel sheets, each linking back
into the screens or states it describes. They share one stylesheet, proto-review.css,
and one contract about file://: a browser may not read sibling files there, so the
pages say so instead of sitting empty.

Underneath, the comment layer itself had five defects that only showed up once it
ran against a live Firebase project rather than being read:

  · A configured prototypeUrl won over the page actually open, so history.replaceState
    threw SecurityError and the pin did nothing on any other origin. There are two
    kinds of link here and now two bases: pageBase() for anything in-page, shareBase()
    only for a link meant to be pasted to somebody else.
  · Three catch blocks discarded the cause, so a rules rejection, a missing document
    and a cross-origin failure all read as one sentence.
  · The error popover kept the last thread's coordinates — measured 9 000 px below
    the fold, so the reviewer saw neither the thread nor the error explaining it.
  · A pin drew on both language siblings, because identical markup means a selector
    written on one resolves on the other. A pin now belongs to its own page.
  · The popover clamped without subtracting its own width, so it ran off the right edge.

Comments are live on Firebase with a named allowlist in Firestore; comments.rules is
the deployed policy and comments.config.json points at the project.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Make the page length a switch: 10 / 20 / 30 results
entries.body:
How long a result page should be is a product question, not a constant. The panel
row "Rezultate pe pagină" (and ?per=10|20|30) moves the list and the pager together:
thirty cards is a long scroll before anyone reaches pagination, ten brings the pager
into the first screen and puts more weight on sorting.

The DOM always holds the full thirty cards — PAGE_SIZE only decides how many are
shown, so the switch is instant and nothing is re-rendered. The visibility cap is now
min(demo inventory, page size), so the demo inventory switch keeps working on top of
it. Read before the export early-return, so a Figma frame can be captured at any page
length.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Make a page of results really hold a page of results, and let the big photo be leafed through
entries.body:
Two things the prototype was claiming but not doing.

The pager says "Afișăm 1–30 din 1 236 cazări" while the list held six hand-written
cards, so the first screen contradicted itself and the demo inventory switch could
never show a full page. fillListingPage() now clones the hand-written cards up to
PAGE_SIZE before anything else in initListing() runs, so every new card gets the
same gallery, filters and room expander. A clone varies what belongs to a property
— name, resort, distance to the beach, stars, score, reviews, price, photo, room
type, quote — and inherits the rest from its source card, so the chips never drift
from the data attributes behind them. The names are real properties from
litoralulromanesc.ro, Mamaia first and then along the coast, which is what the
default "Tot litoralul" search means; in production-photo mode each pulls its own
photos, so a full page also shows how uneven the real photo base is.

The big photo at the top of the hotel page now carries the same arrows as a listing
card, plus a counter, so the property's own photos can be leafed through in place.
Guest photos stay behind the gallery, and clicking the photo still opens the mosaic.

Also fixed on the way: a card with data-disc="0" but an .old-price element rendered
a struck-through "0 Lei" (visible on home-b, and multiplied by the clones); the
strikethrough now hides itself when there is no discount. Hub previews are lazy-loaded
— with 30-card listings the page was pulling ~50 MB of PNGs at once.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Let the prototype run on production photos, at a switch
entries.body:
The prototype ships with clean stock photography, which flatters the layout. The
new "Fotografii — Prototip / Producție" row in the demo panel swaps every image
for the real one from litoralulromanesc.ro, so the design can be judged on the
photo base we actually have: inconsistent crops, portrait phone shots, campaign
badges burned into the JPEG, properties with no spa photo at all. Copy, prices
and behaviour are untouched — only the pictures change.

A hotel card and the hotel page get that property's own photos (the name is read
from the card, so "Complex Mediteranean" shows Complex Mediteranean); the
destination cards get the resort's own photo from the site's gallery; everything
else falls back to a default set picked across properties. All 13 properties the
prototype names by hand exist in production.

The swap sets `srcset` and never rewrites `src`, so every part of proto.js /
proto-m.js that reads or writes `src` — card galleries, the lightbox, the gallery
category map keyed by file name — keeps working untouched, and a MutationObserver
catches images injected later. `?assets=` is read at script-parse time, because
the prototype rewrites its own URL from the search state before DOMContentLoaded
and the parameter would be gone by then.

The pinned campaign card is deliberately left alone: "Super ofertele verii" is
already a production creative. The current campaign banner and the other
creatives are in the pack but unused — the layout has no slot for them yet.

assets/prod/ (13 MB) is generated by tools/scrape-prod-assets.py +
tools/build-prod-assets.py; prod-assets.html is the catalogue of what is in it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Stop the demo panel running off the screen, and let the filters hold their own column
entries.body:
The panel was placed under the "demo inventory" box with getBoundingClientRect,
and that box is centred vertically — so every switch added last round pushed the
panel past the bottom edge of the window. Both boxes now live in one left-hand
rail that scrolls inside itself, so the panel cannot be clipped however many
rows it grows, and a "⚙" pill collapses it into the corner when it would sit
over the page.

The "interactive prototype" hint bar is gone with it: it covered the bottom-left
corner, which is exactly where the prototype controls are.

New switch on the listing: the filter column can stay in view from the map down
and scroll on its own, separately from the results. It steps below the docked
search bar through :has(.ssearch.on), and stays off in export mode so a
full-page capture keeps the whole column.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Give the hotel page the right bar for the right visitor
entries.body:
The two states were swapped on mobile: whoever arrived from our own listing
got a docked summary they no longer need, while a cold visitor got a full
search box pushing the hotel below the fold. Now it reads the way it should
— from our listing, nothing at the top at all; direct arrival, the compact
docked bar, which opens the same search sheet. The big in-page search box is
gone. Desktop already worked this way and is unchanged.

The stay bar in the rooms section now stays put while you scroll rooms —
comparing rooms is exactly when dates and guests need to be one tap away.
Desktop gets it from CSS (sticky inside #camere, which unsticks itself at
the end of the section, sitting under the docked bar when there is one).
Mobile can't: the bar lives in a short section while the room cards are the
next block, so it is fixed from JS over the whole rooms region, with a
spacer holding its place in the flow. Squeezed onto one row it drops
"· 7 nights" and "· 2 rooms" into a <span class="xtra"> the stuck state
hides — the bound spans stay inside, so paint() keeps them current.

Both follow the hotel switch in the prototype panel.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Put the real campaign creative on the pinned card
entries.body:
The banner comes straight off production
(assets/dist/images/header/Banner_ofertele_verii_adela_2*.webp): the wide
1140x260 one for the band, the tighter 856x280 phone one for the card in the
carousel row, where a 4.4:1 strip would crop past readable. The hand-built
lockup it replaces is gone, along with the two script webfonts it needed —
over the creative's own type it would only collide.

Sizes follow the creative, not the other way round: the band keeps its
aspect so nothing is cut, and the pinned card is cropped towards the lockup
(62% on desktop, 66% on mobile, where the card also widens to 88% — below
that the crop eats into "SUPERofertele VERII"). Only the pin marker and the
CTA sit on top, and on the phone band the CTA shrinks so it clears the
creative's own ribbon.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Make the docked bar read as the header, not a white strip on white
entries.body:
Navy background instead of white — on white pages the docked bar simply
disappeared into the content; navy separates it and matches the app bar on
mobile. The search pill keeps the orange border it has in the page.

It also carries what the header carries: the call-centre number with its
hours, the account button (label follows the guest/member switch) and
☰ Meniu. Both open the header's own menus — initHeader now exposes the
openers with the anchor as a parameter, so the bar reuses the panel and the
user menu instead of building copies. Two breakpoints drop the labels, then
the phone, before the 1200px container would push off screen.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Dock the search bar on scroll, and let the first campaign card be pinned
entries.body:
Sticky search: once the big search card leaves the screen, the same three
fields collapse into a bar fixed to the top — minimised but fully working,
since each field opens the very same destination / calendar / guests popover
(moved into the bar through placePop's host argument) and the button reuses
the page's own submit handler. Three independent switches in the prototype
panel — homepage, listing, hotel — kept in localStorage and in the URL
(?sthome=&stlist=&sthotel=), so the same state carries across pages and
between desktop and mobile. On the hotel page the bar follows today's rule:
it only shows for a new visitor. Hidden in export mode (?nopanel=1).

On mobile the homepage gets a search pill docked under the app bar (nothing
was sticky there before), while listing and hotel already dock their summary
— there the switch decides whether it stays, and it now collapses to a
single line as you scroll.

Pinned campaign card: the first slot of the hero carousel can be taken out
of the rotation, so the most important campaign no longer depends on the
autoplay's luck. Two modes on a switch — "Linie" (first card, highlighted,
outside the scroller, the others slide past it) and "Banner" (a wide band
above the carousel). The creative is real text, not a JPG, so it stays
editable in Figma and exists in both languages.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Put the menu back on every mobile screen, and give the desktop one a panel
entries.body:
The hamburger only existed on m-home. Every mobile sub-page header had a
back arrow and no menu at all (thank-you had neither), so from listing,
hotel, checkout and confirmation the whole taxonomy was unreachable —
initHeader() had been wiring a button that was not in the markup.

The burger is now the last item of the bar on all ten mobile pages: back
stays on the left where it exists, and the menu is always the top-right
corner, so its position is the same on every screen.

Same header, two more repairs. The #i-user symbol was never defined on
any mobile page, so the guest account button rendered as an empty box
with a lone orange dot. And on desktop the burger worked but was an
unlabelled icon opening a 900px modal with nine links adrift in white
space, whose href="#" entries did nothing at all — it now reads
"Meniu"/"Menu" and opens an anchored two-column panel with the phone
number in the footer, and the dead links toast like they do on mobile.

tools/serve.js serves the prototype with Cache-Control: no-store, so the
preview pane stops testing a stale proto.js. tools/shoot-previews.js
redoes all sixteen preview-*.png, which a header edit makes stale at once.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Put guest photos under the reviews, and give the phone gallery a mosaic and real zoom
entries.body:
Guest photos and the invitation to add your own now sit below the review cards
instead of above them, on desktop and mobile. The reviews are what a visitor came
to that section for; the pictures read as their continuation rather than as an
interruption of them.

On mobile the second gallery step keeps the mosaic instead of a horizontal
thumbnail strip. A strip under the photo wastes the whole lower half of a phone
screen, so the chosen picture sits above the same mosaic: the selected tile is
ringed, tapping another swaps the photo, and the header's back arrow drops the big
photo before it closes the gallery. Tapping the photo, or the zoom button on it,
opens it full screen with real zoom — pinch, double-tap for 100% to 250%, plus and
minus up to 400%, drag to pan, with panning clamped so the picture cannot be
dragged off screen.

The two guest-content buttons on mobile now share one row instead of stacking, so
the block costs half the vertical space.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Open the gallery as a mosaic, put guest photos in the reviews, give documents a state
entries.body:
Three changes across desktop and mobile, RO and EN.

Gallery in two steps: clicking any photo opens a mosaic of every picture first,
with category chips and counts (including "from guests"); clicking a tile switches
to the big image with a horizontal thumbnail strip, arrow keys and a way back to
the mosaic. A side rail keeps the score, two guest quotes and the price with a
"see the rooms" CTA visible in both steps, so the gallery sells instead of parking
the visitor. Mobile runs the same two steps in a full-screen sheet, where the
header's back arrow goes mosaic-ward first and only closes from the mosaic.

Photos and clips from guests: a named block in the reviews section with uploader
names, video duration badges and a "+42" tile, review cards carrying their own
photos and a verified-stay line, and everything opening the same gallery filtered
on guest content. "Add photos or clips" and "Write a review" are mockup flows with
a drop zone, a prunable file list, inline attachments that do not lose typed text,
and an unticked consent that gates the send button — the same rule as checkout.
The first published set earns +20 FRIENDS credits, because guest content only
exists if there is a reason to upload it.

Documents carry their state: a green tick for what is ready now, a gray hourglass
on a dashed row for what is issued later, with the action reading Download or
Coming soon / At check-in, plus a legend. After paying, the open question is what
you have and what you are still waiting for.

Also fixes a hardcoded Romanian "+78 fotografii" in the CSS that leaked onto the
English hotel page; the label is now injected in the page language.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Start from the whole coast on any cold entry, not just for first-time visitors
entries.body:
The all-resorts default only reached people with no stored session. Anyone who
had used the prototype before still had "Mamaia" saved, so the search field kept
showing it and the change looked like it had not landed.

Entering without a dest parameter — from Google, from a shared link, from the
overview page — now starts from the whole coast regardless of what the session
remembers. Navigation inside the prototype always carries dest in the query
string, so a search you actually ran is still carried from screen to screen.
Verified both directions: cold entry gives "Cazare pe tot litoralul", and
?dest=Eforie Nord still gives "Cazare Eforie Nord".

An earlier attempt versioned the stored state and expired old sessions once.
Dropped: it silently destroys someone's session, its effect depends on load
order, and it cannot be verified without a persistent browser profile. The
URL rule does the same job and is observable in one page load.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Stop the hero clipping the search popovers; make the all-resorts default actually stick
entries.body:
The search hero carried overflow:hidden to round its background image, which
also clipped the destination, calendar and guests popovers at its bottom edge —
on the homepage the dropdown was cut to a sliver. The rounding moved to the
background layer, so the hero clips the photo and nothing else.

The all-resorts default only applied to fresh visitors. Anyone who had opened
the prototype before still had "Mamaia" in their stored session and saw it in
the search field, which reads as the default not having changed. The state now
carries a version marker and a stale one is dropped once. The static markup also
said Mamaia before the engine painted over it, on both platforms and in both
languages — it now says "Tot litoralul" / "All resorts".

Found while checking the fix: the desktop destination picker was hardcoded in
Romanian, so the English pages listed "319 cazări" under an English placeholder.
Both go through the language helper now.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Search the whole coast by default, cleaner listing headline, two new demo switches
entries.body:
Search & homepage. The search now covers all resorts at once instead of making
someone pick one first: "Tot litoralul" is the preselected destination and the
first row in the picker, dropping out once you start typing a resort name. An
empty dest means all resorts throughout both engines, so the listing headline
reads "Cazare pe tot litoralul" and the demo inventory tops out at 1,236 — the
whole coast — rather than Mamaia's 81.

Listing. The headline carried the site-wide review score next to the place name
("Stays in Mamaia 8.7/10 from 11,395 reviews"), which said nothing about the
result set; it now carries the count and nothing else. The room-type expander on
the cards can be switched off from the prototype panel, desktop and mobile.

Hotel page. Someone landing cold — from Google, from an ad — has not searched
anything yet, so the search bar is back on top for them; someone who arrived
from a listing has already searched and the same bar would only pull them out of
the flow. Which case you are looking at is a switch in the panel, "Sesiune:
vizitator nou / de pe site", and a ?session= parameter.

Also on the hotel page, below the map: "De ce să rezervi prin noi" — the agency
facts that were only ever on the homepage, where the decision is not being made.
500+ directly contracted properties, licensed since 2005, 270,000 tourists in
2024, 0% instalments, three holiday cards, consultants daily 10–18.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Frame the charter cards instead of tinting them; fix two sidebar problems
entries.body:
Three fixes from looking at the live listing.

The map card sat flush against the "Garantat de noi" button — it now takes the
same 12px gap the filter boxes use.

The availability box carried a blue highlight left over from an earlier round.
With the charter toggle above it, two accents competed and the one drawing the
eye was the one that mattered least; availability is a plain box now, and the
only accent in the rail belongs to the charter set.

The tint on charter cards was too weak to sell anything — it read as a row
selected with Tab. Replaced by a navy frame: 2px border plus a soft halo, badge
in the tag row. A full-width ribbon across the card head was tried first and
dropped: at six cards in a column it turned the page into stripes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Paginate the listing at 30 per page instead of load-more
entries.body:
"Afișează mai multe rezultate" hid two things at once: how much is left and
where you are in the list. Infinite scroll would have added a third — it buries
the footer and makes a result you scrolled past impossible to return to. Both
listings now carry a pager with a range line, "Afișăm 1–30 din 81 cazări",
built from the result count so desktop and mobile stay in step. Below 31 results
the whole block hides itself, so a filtered set of three gets no decoration.

Two things had to be fixed for the count to mean anything. The desktop listing
shipped with the "Piscină" filter pre-checked, which pinned the headline at four
results and put the page into the low-inventory treatment on first load; the
preset is gone, and the filter chips still demo themselves the moment anything
is ticked. The desktop demo-inventory switcher also had no initial state, so the
listing reported the six demo cards rather than the size of the result set —
it now reads the first tier at init, the way mobile already did.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Reorder the listing filters, add a zero-inventory view, sign-in, and a filtered entry point
entries.body:
Filter rail, in the order agreed at the workshop: map, then a big "Garantat de
noi" toggle, recent filters, popular filters, availability trimmed to the two
rows that matter (bookable, instantly confirmed), the price histogram, then
review score, board, property type, payment and cancellation, discounts,
holiday card and the rest. The order lives in the engine, so Romanian and
English cannot drift apart. The mobile filter sheet follows the same taxonomy,
with the charter toggle at the top and the histogram in the same position.

The demo switcher gains a zero-inventory tier. That exposed duplicate messaging:
the empty-state box and the static rescue band were both talking. The band now
stands down at zero, and the empty state distinguishes its two causes — filters
too tight versus nothing free for these dates — because the way out differs.

Charter cards get a light navy tint and a hairline border on top of the left
accent, so the set reads as a group when scanning.

Signing in was missing entirely — the prototype could only offer to join
FRIENDS. Added an account button in the mobile app bar, a proper button in the
desktop header for guests, and a homepage band that disappears for members; all
three open the same sign-in / create-account sheet, which states what an account
is actually for. Fields are mock placeholders.

The "see all guaranteed hotels" link now opens the listing already filtered via
?f=own. The parameter clears the page's preset filters first, so the link lands
on one intention rather than an accidental intersection.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Make the rescue widgets inventory-aware, fix the pre-selection CTA, add the charter set
entries.body:
Three things from the workshop.

1. The anti-dead-end widgets did not react to how many results were left. The
   flexible-date strip did; the call-centre band, the nearby-resorts band and
   "load more" were static markup, always on. They are now driven by the visible
   result count, on desktop and mobile alike: above 5 stays they stay out of the
   way, at 5 or fewer the date strip, a "look at other options" line and the
   nearby band appear while "load more" and the pager go, and at 2 or fewer the
   call-centre band moves directly under the last result, turns orange and names
   the number left. The headline also switches from the general review score to
   the real count. The desktop demo tiers capped at 6, which with six demo cards
   changed nothing — they now cap at 4 and 2 so the states are actually visible.

2. Before a room is picked there is nothing to book, so the desktop hotel CTA no
   longer says "Rezervă acum" / "Book now". It says "Alege camera" / "Choose a
   room", scrolls to the room picker and highlights it. Mobile already did this.

3. The hotels we charter are now a first-class, promotable set. data-own="1" on
   a card gets a navy "Garantat de noi" badge and a navy accent; the badge opens
   an explainer covering what actually differs — real availability from our own
   allotment, instant confirmation, and consultants who can change the booking
   without the hotel. The homepage gets a "Hoteluri garantate de noi" row on
   desktop and mobile, the listing gets a matching filter, and the default
   "Recomandate de noi" sort puts the set first.

All of it in Romanian and English. litro-final.fig regenerated from the 35
frames; previews refreshed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Add litro-final.fig — one Figma file with every screen and state variant
entries.body:
35 editable frames on a single canvas, laid out in labelled rows: the desktop
flow in Romanian and English, the desktop state variants, the archived A/B
homepages and listings, the mobile flow in both languages, and the mobile state
variants. 22,698 layers, 134 images; round-trip validated through the repo's own
decoder and renderer, data chunk is zstd.

To capture the states deterministically the prototypes now read them from the
URL — on desktop and mobile alike:

  ?auth=in|out      member vs guest (hides the "sign in for FRIENDS" bands)
  ?density=a|b|c    listing card density
  ?inv=many|some|few  demo inventory (mobile listing)
  ?room=2           pre-selects rooms so the booking bar is up (mobile hotel)
  ?nopanel=1        export mode

That doubles as a product nicety: any state can now be linked to directly.

Export mode also had to hide the demo chrome that is part of the page rather
than the floating panel — the desktop inventory box and variant switcher — and
neutralise position:fixed elements. A fixed bar is captured at the bottom edge
of the 1200px capture window, which lands in the middle of a 4000px frame; in
export mode those bars join the normal flow instead. Without this the last
export carried the inventory panel and a stray booking bar across twelve
desktop frames.

tools/dump-all.sh dumps all 35 frames; tools/generate-fig-all.js lays them out,
computing row offsets from the dumps so nothing overlaps.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Add the mobile Figma export and fix the search-summary card layout
entries.body:
litro-mobile-web.fig — a native Figma file with all ten mobile screens as
editable 430px frames, Romanian on the top row and English below. Round-trip
validated through the repo's own decoder and renderer; the data chunk is zstd
(deflate makes Figma's importer hang silently at "0 of 1 files").

Pipeline changes:
- dump-dom.js takes an optional viewport width (still 1440 by default).
- generate-fig-m.js is the 430px variant of generate-fig.js, with an `oy` field
  so the frames can sit in two rows.
- ?nopanel=1 puts the prototype in export mode: the floating demo panel is not
  built and the fixed bottom bars join the normal flow. Without it the bars are
  captured at the bottom of the 1200px capture window — the middle of the frame.

Found while exporting: in the search-summary card the name and the date line
were inline spans, so a long hotel name pushed the dates onto a second line that
overlapped the title. They are block-level now, which is also how the approved
Mobile (REDESIGN) frames draw that card — name on top, context underneath.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Add the mobile web flow (RO + EN) and a desktop/mobile prototype switch
entries.body:
Five mobile screens at 390px — home, listing, hotel, checkout, confirmation —
rebuilt from the desktop C flow and the approved "Mobile (REDESIGN)" frames in
the LITRO Master Pages Figma file: navy app bar, the white search-summary card
with the orange border, the Filters / Sort / Map row, the 3-step checkout
stepper and the editable advance.

- litro-m.css repeats the same :root token block as litro.css and then defines
  only mobile components; litro.css stays the source of truth for tokens.
- proto-m.js is a separate engine but shares the "litro" localStorage key and
  the price model with proto.js, so state and prices carry across desktop and
  mobile. Fully bilingual through t(ro, en); navigation resolves the -en pages.
- Mobile-only interaction: full-screen sheets for search, calendar, guests,
  filters and sort; a swipeable hotel gallery; a booking bar that slides up
  after the first room is added; a fixed checkout bar with the amount due today.
- Demo switches live in one floating "Prototype · settings" panel rather than in
  the page: language, desktop/mobile view, guest/member, card density (A
  detailed / B compact with icons / C horizontal summary) and demo inventory.
- proto.js gains the same View row on desktop, so the phone screens are
  reachable from a full-size browser window and back, carrying dest and dates.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Shorter C cards, orange guided checkout CTA, logged-in/out prototype switch
entries.body:
- Card view C: compact the right column (cancel the margin-top:auto that stretched
  it, smaller price/CTA, tighter icons, shorter photo) so the card is ~185px vs
  222 (B) / 276 (A) — less empty space.
- Checkout summary CTA is now always orange (not greyed); clicking it walks the
  user through the form sections one by one (highlighting each) and, once consent
  is ticked, proceeds to the confirmation page. The bottom form CTA keeps its
  consent gating.
- Prototype panel gains an Account switch (Guest / Member). Member hides the
  'sign in for the FRIENDS discount' banners (.friends-band, .loyal-band) and the
  header shows 'Ana'; Guest shows the banners and 'Sign in'. State persists in
  localStorage across the flow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Fix card density modes, dock prototype panel under inventory demo, checkout CTA in first viewport
entries.body:
- Card density: A = detailed, B = compact (previous B: no quote/perks, plus now
  no '2 adults…/VAT…' price note; keeps room + tags), C = big-icon summary (the
  former B). Relabel C as Icons/Iconițe.
- Dock the floating 'Prototype · settings' panel right below the inventory-demo
  box (measured from .invdemo, repositioned on resize); rows stacked to fit.
- Checkout: add a booking CTA inside the sticky summary card, placed right under
  the total (before the 'to pay at the hotel' block) with a shorter summary photo
  so it sits in the first viewport (~737px). It mirrors the consent gating of the
  main CTA and scrolls to the consent box when still disabled.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Listing: icon-based Compact card view, prototype-controls panel, reordered filters
entries.body:
- Compact (B) card view now shows a big-icon summary (date/nights · meal · room),
  like the reference screenshot, and drops the '2 adults, 7 nights…/VAT…' note.
  A = detailed, B = compact (icons), C = minimal.
- Move the RO/EN language switch and the A/B/C card-view switch into a floating
  'Prototype · settings' panel styled like the inventory-demo box — they are demo
  controls, not product UI. Header langswitch hidden (via .header .langswitch to
  beat the inline style on home-c/home-d).
- Reorder the listing filter sidebar: Recent + Popular (compacted) on top,
  Availability lower, the rest unchanged. Done at runtime in initListing so it
  applies to listing-c and home-d in both languages.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Hotel: drop nearby-alternatives band; listings: remove type chips + count strip; sticky checkout summary; A/B/C card density switch
entries.body:
- Hotel (RO+EN): remove the 'Nearby alternatives, from our inventory' section so
  we don't derail the user off the chosen hotel.
- Listing (RO+EN): drop the res-types chips (Hotels/Apartments/Rooms) and the
  'X available stays' count; the header now shows only the review score (data-fixed
  so applyFilters no longer re-adds the count).
- Checkout: the right-hand summary column is now position:sticky.
- Listing card density switch A/B/C (injected in initListing, RO/EN labels):
  A = detailed (as now), B = compact (no quote/perks), C = minimal (name, meta,
  rating, price, CTA only). Cards were too heavy; B/C slim them down.
